note: Event cards typed by Orbis. Dates: astronomical years (1 BC = 0); ancient dates before 45 BC follow the Roman tradition and are given as years only. Each card names its source (an ancient author and/or the Wikipedia article).

items.title: Adrianople
items.text: Goths destroyed an eastern Roman army and killed the emperor Valens.

items.title: The Rhine crossing
items.text: Vandals, Alans and Suebi crossed the Rhine near Mogontiacum (Mainz) at the end of 406 and moved on into Gaul and Spain.

items.title: Rome sacked
items.text: Alaric's Visigoths plundered Rome for three days, the first time in 800 years an enemy had taken the city.

items.title: Vandals take Carthage
items.text: The Vandals took Carthage and Rome's richest grain provinces in Africa.

items.title: Attila stopped
items.text: Romans and Visigoths fought Attila's Huns to a halt in Gaul at the Catalaunian Plains; the exact site is unknown.
items.source: Jordanes, Getica; Wikipedia 'Battle of the Catalaunian Plains'

items.title: The last western emperor
items.text: The general Odoacer deposed the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus at Ravenna and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople.

items.title: Justinian's wars
items.text: Belisarius retook Africa from the Vandals in 533–534; Italy followed after a 20-year war with the Ostrogoths, and part of southern Spain in 552.

items.title: Lombards in Italy
items.text: The Lombards invaded Italy; Constantinople kept only Ravenna, Rome, the south and the islands.

items.title: Yarmouk
items.text: Arab armies defeated the Romans in Syria. Within six years Syria, Palestine and Egypt were lost.

items.title: Carthage falls
items.text: The Umayyads took Carthage, ending Roman rule in Africa.

items.title: A new western emperor
items.text: The pope crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne emperor in Rome. Constantinople did not recognise the title.

items.title: Manzikert
items.text: The Seljuk Turks defeated and captured the emperor Romanos IV; Anatolia lay open to Turkish settlement.

items.title: Crusaders take Constantinople
items.text: The Fourth Crusade sacked the city and set up a Latin Empire. Byzantine rulers won it back in 1261.

items.title: Constantinople falls
items.text: Mehmed II's Ottoman army took the city after a siege of 53 days, on 29 May 1453 by the Julian calendar then in use (7 June in today's calendar). The last emperor, Constantine XI, died in the fighting.

items.title: Trebizond
items.text: The Ottomans took Trebizond on the Black Sea, the last Greek state that claimed the Roman succession.
